Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: All cells reproduce by dividing into two, with each parental cell giving rise to two daughter cells each time they divide.

Reason: Each parental cell divides into exactly two daughters, conserving genetic information without dilution.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed cell cycle.

Reason: The cell cycle is the complete sequence of events that doubles a cell's contents and then distributes them equally into two daughters.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage in the cell cycle.
False 1: DNA synthesis occurs during all stages of the cell cycle.
FIB 1: DNA ___ occurs only during one specific stage in the cell cycle.
FIB 2: DNA synthesis occurs only during one ___ stage in the cell cycle.
FIB 3: DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage in the cell ___.
Reason: DNA synthesis is restricted to the S phase so that each chromosome is replicated exactly once per cell cycle.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Human cells in culture divide once in approximately every 24 hours.
False 1: Human cells in culture divide once in approximately every 90 minutes.
False 2: Yeast cells divide once in approximately every 24 hours.
FIB 1: Human cells in ___ divide once in approximately every 24 hours.
FIB 2: Human cells in culture divide once in ___ every 24 hours.
FIB 3: Human cells in culture divide once in approximately every ___ hours.
Reason: Human cells are large and complex, requiring ~24 hours to replicate all 6 billion base pairs and complete mitosis.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Yeast can progress through the cell cycle in only about 90 minutes.
False 1: Yeast can progress through the cell cycle in only about 24 hours.
FIB 1: Yeast can ___ through the cell cycle in only about 90 minutes.
FIB 2: Yeast can progress through the cell cycle in only about ___ minutes.
FIB 3: Yeast can progress through the cell cycle in only about 90 ___.
Reason: Yeast cells are small and genetically simple; their streamlined metabolism allows very rapid cell cycle completion.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: Interphase and M Phase (Mitosis phase).
False 1: The cell cycle is divided into four basic phases: G₁, S, G₂, and M Phase.
FIB 1: The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: ___ and M Phase (Mitosis phase).
FIB 2: The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: Interphase and M ___ (Mitosis phase).
FIB 3: The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: Interphase and M Phase (___ phase).
Reason: The cell cycle has two main phases: interphase (preparation) and M phase (execution of division).

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The M Phase represents the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs.
False 1: The interphase represents the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs.
FIB 1: The M ___ represents the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs.
FIB 2: The M Phase ___ the phase when the actual cell division or mitosis occurs.
FIB 3: The M Phase represents the phase when the actual cell division or ___ occurs.
Reason: The M phase is when DNA is physically separated into two sets and the cell physically divides.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The interphase represents the phase between two successive M phases.
False 1: The M Phase represents the phase between two successive interphases.
FIB 1: The ___ represents the phase between two successive M phases.
FIB 2: The interphase ___ the phase between two successive M phases.
FIB 3: The interphase represents the phase between two ___ M phases.
Reason: Interphase is the period between two divisions during which all the preparation for the next division occurs.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: In the 24 hour average duration of cell cycle of a human cell, cell division proper lasts for only about an hour.
False 1: In the 24 hour average duration of cell cycle of a human cell, cell division proper lasts for about 12 hours.
FIB 1: In the ___ hour average duration of cell cycle of a human cell, cell division proper lasts for only about an hour.
FIB 2: In the 24 hour average ___ of cell cycle of a human cell, cell division proper lasts for only about an hour.
FIB 3: In the 24 hour average duration of cell cycle of a human cell, cell ___ proper lasts for only about an hour.
Reason: The 24-hour cycle allocates only ~1 hour for M phase because the actual chromosome separation is fast once the cell is prepared.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The interphase lasts more than 95% of the duration of cell cycle.
False 1: The M Phase lasts more than 95% of the duration of cell cycle.
FIB 1: The ___ lasts more than 95% of the duration of cell cycle.
FIB 2: The interphase lasts more than ___% of the duration of cell cycle.
FIB 3: The interphase lasts more than 95% of the ___ of cell cycle.
Reason: Interphase occupies >95% of the cell cycle because duplicating the entire genome and all cellular contents takes much longer than the physical separation.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The M Phase starts with the nuclear division (karyokinesis) and usually ends with division of cytoplasm (cytokinesis).
False 1: The M Phase starts with division of cytoplasm (cytokinesis) and usually ends with nuclear division (karyokinesis).
FIB 1: The M ___ starts with the nuclear division (karyokinesis) and usually ends with division of cytoplasm (cytokinesis).
FIB 2: The M Phase starts with the nuclear division (___) and usually ends with division of cytoplasm (cytokinesis).
FIB 3: The M Phase starts with the nuclear division (karyokinesis) and usually ends with division of cytoplasm (___).
Reason: Karyokinesis (nuclear division) must precede cytokinesis (cytoplasmic division) so that each daughter cell receives a complete nucleus.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The interphase is divided into three further phases: G₁ phase (Gap 1), S phase (Synthesis), G₂ phase (Gap 2).
False 1: The interphase is divided into four further phases: G₁, S, G₂, and G₀.
FIB 1: The ___ is divided into three further phases: G₁ phase (Gap 1), S phase (Synthesis), G₂ phase (Gap 2).
FIB 2: The interphase is divided into three further phases: ___ phase (Gap 1), S phase (Synthesis), G₂ phase (Gap 2).
FIB 3: The interphase is divided into three further phases: G₁ phase (Gap 1), S phase (Synthesis), ___ phase (Gap 2).
Reason: Interphase is subdivided into G₁ (growth), S (DNA synthesis) and G₂ (preparation for division) to ensure all components are doubled in order.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: G₁ phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication.
False 1: S phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication.
FIB 1: ___ phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication.
FIB 2: G₁ phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of ___ replication.
FIB 3: G₁ phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA ___.
Reason: G₁ is the gap between the previous mitosis and DNA replication during which the cell grows and checks that conditions are right for DNA synthesis.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During G₁ phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.
False 1: During S phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.
FIB 1: During ___ phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA.
FIB 2: During G₁ phase, the cell is metabolically active and ___ grows but does not replicate its DNA.
FIB 3: During G₁ phase, the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its ___.
Reason: During G₁, the cell grows and synthesises proteins but withholds DNA replication until it passes the G₁ checkpoint.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place.
False 1: G₁ or gap phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place.
FIB 1: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which ___ synthesis or replication takes place.
FIB 2: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA ___ or replication takes place.
FIB 3: S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or ___ takes place.
Reason: S phase is dedicated exclusively to DNA synthesis, doubling the genetic content from 2C to 4C.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During S phase, the amount of DNA per cell doubles.
False 1: During S phase, the amount of DNA per cell halves.
FIB 1: During S phase, the amount of ___ per cell doubles.
FIB 2: During S phase, the amount of DNA per ___ doubles.
FIB 3: During S phase, the amount of DNA per cell ___.
Reason: DNA replication in S phase doubles the amount of DNA (2C → 4C) while chromosome number stays the same because replicated strands remain joined at the centromere.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: If the initial amount of DNA is 2C then it increases to 4C during S phase.
False 1: If the initial amount of DNA is 2C then it increases to 3C during S phase.
FIB 1: If the initial amount of ___ is 2C then it increases to 4C during S phase.
FIB 2: If the initial amount of DNA is ___ then it increases to 4C during S phase.
FIB 3: If the initial amount of DNA is 2C then it increases to ___ during S phase.
Reason: Each chromosome's DNA is replicated exactly once in S phase, doubling DNA content from 2C to 4C, with the two copies held together as sister chromatids.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: There is no increase in the chromosome number during S phase.
False 1: There is a doubling of chromosome number during S phase.
FIB 1: ___ is no increase in the chromosome number during S phase.
FIB 2: There is no ___ in the chromosome number during S phase.
FIB 3: There is no increase in the ___ number during S phase.
Reason: Chromosome number remains 2n after S phase because sister chromatids are held together at the centromere and counted as one chromosome.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: If the cell had diploid (2n) number of chromosomes at G₁, after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n.
False 1: If the cell had diploid (2n) number of chromosomes at G₁, after S phase the number of chromosomes doubles to 4n.
FIB 1: If the cell had diploid (2n) number of chromosomes at ___, after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n.
FIB 2: If the cell had diploid (2n) number of chromosomes at G₁, after S phase the number of ___ remains the same, i.e., 2n.
FIB 3: If the cell had diploid (2n) number of chromosomes at G₁, after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., ___.
Reason: Chromosome number stays 2n after S phase because each chromosome now consists of two identical sister chromatids joined at the centromere, not two separate chromosomes.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.
False 1: In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the cytoplasm, and the centriole duplicates in the nucleus.
False 2: In animal cells, during the G₂ phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.
FIB 1: In animal cells, during the S phase, ___ replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.
FIB 2: In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA ___ begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm.
FIB 3: In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole ___ in the cytoplasm.
Reason: Centriole duplication in S phase ensures that each pole of the mitotic spindle will have a centrosome when the cell enters M phase.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During the G₂ phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.
False 1: During the S phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.
FIB 1: During the ___ phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.
FIB 2: During the G₂ phase, proteins are ___ in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues.
FIB 3: During the G₂ phase, proteins are synthesised in ___ for mitosis while cell growth continues.
Reason: G₂ proteins include tubulin (for spindle assembly), condensins (for chromosome compaction) and mitotic kinases that trigger M phase entry.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Cells that do not divide further exit G₁ phase to enter an inactive stage called quiescent stage (G₀) of the cell cycle.
False 1: Cells that do not divide further exit S phase to enter an inactive stage called quiescent stage (G₀) of the cell cycle.
FIB 1: Cells that do not divide further exit ___ phase to enter an inactive stage called quiescent stage (G₀) of the cell cycle.
FIB 2: Cells that do not divide further exit G₁ phase to enter an inactive stage called ___ stage (G₀) of the cell cycle.
FIB 3: Cells that do not divide further exit G₁ phase to enter an inactive stage called quiescent stage (___) of the cell cycle.
Reason: Cells exit the cell cycle at G₁ when growth signals are absent; once in G₀, they remain functional but stop dividing.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Cells in G₀ stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate.
False 1: Cells in G₀ stage remain metabolically inactive and no longer proliferate.
FIB 1: Cells in ___ stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate.
FIB 2: Cells in G₀ stage remain ___ active but no longer proliferate.
FIB 3: Cells in G₀ stage remain metabolically active but no longer ___.
Reason: G₀ cells are metabolically active because they still carry out their tissue-specific functions, just not DNA replication or division.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: In animals, mitotic cell division is only seen in the diploid somatic cells.
False 1: In animals, mitotic cell division is seen in both haploid and diploid somatic cells.
FIB 1: In animals, mitotic cell ___ is only seen in the diploid somatic cells.
FIB 2: In animals, mitotic cell division is only seen in the ___ somatic cells.
FIB 3: In animals, mitotic cell division is only seen in the diploid ___ cells.
Reason: Mitosis occurs only in diploid somatic cells because it conserves the diploid chromosome number needed for body function.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Male honey bees are an exception where haploid cells divide by mitosis.
False 1: Female honey bees are an exception where haploid cells divide by mitosis.
FIB 1: Male honey bees are an ___ where haploid cells divide by mitosis.
FIB 2: Male honey bees are an exception where ___ cells divide by mitosis.
FIB 3: Male honey bees are an exception where haploid cells divide by ___.
Reason: Male honey bees (drones) develop parthenogenetically from unfertilised haploid eggs, so their cells are haploid but still divide by mitosis to build the organism.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Plants can show mitotic divisions in both haploid and diploid cells.
False 1: Plants can show mitotic divisions only in diploid cells.
FIB 1: Plants can show mitotic ___ in both haploid and diploid cells.
FIB 2: Plants can show mitotic divisions in both ___ and diploid cells.
FIB 3: Plants can show mitotic divisions in both haploid and ___ cells.
Reason: Plants can mitose in haploid gametophyte tissue (e.g., pollen grains, prothallus) as well as in diploid sporophyte tissue.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Since the number of chromosomes in the parent and progeny cells is the same, mitosis is called equational division.
False 1: Since the number of chromosomes in the parent and progeny cells is the same, meiosis is called equational division.
FIB 1: Since the number of ___ in the parent and progeny cells is the same, mitosis is called equational division.
FIB 2: Since the number of chromosomes in the parent and progeny cells is the same, mitosis is called ___ division.
FIB 3: Since the number of chromosomes in the parent and progeny cells is the same, mitosis is called equational ___.
Reason: Mitosis is equational because the chromosome number (2n) is maintained in both daughter cells, unlike meiosis which halves it.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Karyokinesis involves four stages: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and Telophase.
False 1: Karyokinesis involves three stages: Prophase, Metaphase, and Telophase.
FIB 1: Karyokinesis involves four stages: Prophase, ___, Anaphase, and Telophase.
FIB 2: Karyokinesis involves four stages: Prophase, Metaphase, ___, and Telophase.
FIB 3: Karyokinesis involves four stages: Prophase, Metaphase, Anaphase, and ___.
Reason: Karyokinesis (nuclear division) consists of four stages because chromosomes must be condensed, aligned, separated and then decondensed in an orderly sequence.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Prophase is the first stage of karyokinesis of mitosis.
False 1: Metaphase is the first stage of karyokinesis of mitosis.
FIB 1: ___ is the first stage of karyokinesis of mitosis.
FIB 2: Prophase is the first stage of ___ of mitosis.
FIB 3: Prophase is the first stage of karyokinesis of ___.
Reason: Prophase is the first and longest stage of mitosis because chromosome condensation, spindle formation and nuclear envelope breakdown take time.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Prophase follows the S and G₂ phases of interphase.
False 1: Prophase follows the G₁ and S phases of interphase.
FIB 1: ___ follows the S and G₂ phases of interphase.
FIB 2: Prophase follows the S and ___ phases of interphase.
FIB 3: Prophase follows the S and G₂ phases of ___.
Reason: Prophase follows G₂ because all DNA replication and protein synthesis needed for mitosis must be complete before chromosome condensation begins.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Prophase is marked by the initiation of condensation of chromosomal material.
False 1: Metaphase is marked by the initiation of condensation of chromosomal material.
FIB 1: Prophase is marked by the ___ of condensation of chromosomal material.
FIB 2: Prophase is marked by the initiation of ___ of chromosomal material.
FIB 3: Prophase is marked by the initiation of condensation of ___ material.
Reason: Chromosome condensation in prophase is essential because long, uncondensed chromatin fibres cannot be pulled to the poles without tangling.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The centrosome, which had undergone duplication during S phase of interphase, begins to move towards opposite poles of the cell during prophase.
False 1: The centrosome, which had undergone duplication during G₂ phase of interphase, begins to move towards opposite poles of the cell during prophase.
FIB 1: The ___, which had undergone duplication during S phase of interphase, begins to move towards opposite poles of the cell during prophase.
FIB 2: The centrosome, which had undergone ___ during S phase of interphase, begins to move towards opposite poles of the cell during prophase.
FIB 3: The centrosome, which had undergone duplication during S phase of ___, begins to move towards opposite poles of the cell during prophase.
Reason: The centrosome duplicated in S phase migrates to the poles during prophase so that spindle fibres can radiate from each pole.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Each centrosome radiates out microtubules called asters.
False 1: Each kinetochore radiates out microtubules called asters.
FIB 1: Each ___ radiates out microtubules called asters.
FIB 2: Each centrosome ___ out microtubules called asters.
FIB 3: Each centrosome radiates out ___ called asters.
Reason: Asters (star-shaped microtubule arrays) radiate from each centrosome and help position the mitotic spindle within the cell.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The two asters together with spindle fibres form the mitotic apparatus.
False 1: The two kinetochores together with spindle fibres form the mitotic apparatus.
FIB 1: The two asters together with ___ fibres form the mitotic apparatus.
FIB 2: The two asters together with spindle fibres form the ___ apparatus.
FIB 3: The two asters together with spindle fibres form the mitotic ___.
Reason: Two asters + spindle fibres = the mitotic apparatus that captures, aligns and separates chromosomes during M phase.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Cells at the end of prophase do not show golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus and the nuclear envelope.
False 1: Cells at the end of metaphase do not show golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus and the nuclear envelope.
FIB 1: Cells at the end of prophase do not show golgi complexes, ___ reticulum, nucleolus and the nuclear envelope.
FIB 2: Cells at the end of prophase do not show golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus and the ___ envelope.
FIB 3: Cells at the end of prophase do not show golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus and the nuclear ___.
Reason: Golgi, ER, nucleolus and nuclear envelope disappear at the end of prophase to give chromosomes unobstructed access to the spindle fibres.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Chromosomes at prophase are seen to be composed of two chromatids attached together at the centromere.
False 1: Chromosomes at prophase are seen to be composed of four chromatids attached together at the centromere.
False 2: Chromosomes at prophase are seen to be composed of two chromatids attached together at the kinetochore.
FIB 1: ___ at prophase are seen to be composed of two chromatids attached together at the centromere.
FIB 2: Chromosomes at prophase are seen to be composed of two ___ attached together at the centromere.
FIB 3: Chromosomes at prophase are seen to be composed of two chromatids attached together at the ___.
Reason: Each chromosome entering mitosis consists of two sister chromatids, the products of S-phase DNA replication, joined at the centromere.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of metaphase.
False 1: The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of anaphase.
FIB 1: The complete ___ of the nuclear envelope marks the start of metaphase.
FIB 2: The complete disintegration of the nuclear ___ marks the start of metaphase.
FIB 3: The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of ___.
Reason: Nuclear envelope breakdown at the metaphase transition allows spindle microtubules to reach and capture chromosomes.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: By metaphase, condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be clearly observed under the microscope.
False 1: By prophase, condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be clearly observed under the microscope.
FIB 1: By metaphase, ___ of chromosomes is completed and they can be clearly observed under the microscope.
FIB 2: By metaphase, condensation of ___ is completed and they can be clearly observed under the microscope.
FIB 3: By metaphase, condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be clearly observed under the ___.
Reason: Chromosomes are maximally condensed at metaphase, making them shortest and thickest — ideal for karyotyping because individual chromosomes are clearly resolvable.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Metaphase is the stage at which morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied.
False 1: Prophase is the stage at which morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied.
FIB 1: ___ is the stage at which morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied.
FIB 2: Metaphase is the stage at which ___ of chromosomes is most easily studied.
FIB 3: Metaphase is the stage at which morphology of ___ is most easily studied.
Reason: Metaphase is used for karyotyping because chromosomes are most condensed and individually distinguishable at this stage.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At metaphase, the chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere.
False 1: At metaphase, the chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the kinetochore.
FIB 1: At metaphase, the ___ is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere.
FIB 2: At metaphase, the chromosome is made up of two sister ___, which are held together by the centromere.
FIB 3: At metaphase, the chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the ___.
Reason: Each chromosome at metaphase is a structure of two sister chromatids held at the centromere, forming an X shape visible under the microscope.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores.
False 1: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called asters.
FIB 1: Small disc-shaped ___ at the surface of the centromeres are called kinetochores.
FIB 2: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the ___ are called kinetochores.
FIB 3: Small disc-shaped structures at the surface of the centromeres are called ___.
Reason: Kinetochores are protein complexes assembled on centromere DNA that act as docking sites for spindle microtubules.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Kinetochores serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres to the chromosomes.
False 1: Centromeres serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres to the chromosomes.
FIB 1: ___ serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres to the chromosomes.
FIB 2: Kinetochores serve as the sites of ___ of spindle fibres to the chromosomes.
FIB 3: Kinetochores serve as the sites of attachment of spindle fibres to the ___.
Reason: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores (not directly to centromeres) so that pulling force is transmitted accurately to each chromatid.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At metaphase, one chromatid of each chromosome is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole.
False 1: At metaphase, one chromatid of each chromosome is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the same pole.
FIB 1: At metaphase, one chromatid of each ___ is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole.
FIB 2: At metaphase, one chromatid of each chromosome is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid is connected by its ___ to spindle fibres from the opposite pole.
FIB 3: At metaphase, one chromatid of each chromosome is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid is connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the ___ pole.
Reason: Amphitelic attachment (one kinetochore to each pole) creates balanced tension that places chromosomes on the equatorial plate.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The plane of alignment of the chromosomes at metaphase is referred to as the metaphase plate.
False 1: The plane of alignment of the chromosomes at anaphase is referred to as the metaphase plate.
FIB 1: The plane of alignment of the ___ at metaphase is referred to as the metaphase plate.
FIB 2: The plane of alignment of the chromosomes at metaphase is ___ to as the metaphase plate.
FIB 3: The plane of alignment of the chromosomes at metaphase is referred to as the ___ plate.
Reason: The metaphase plate is a virtual plane defined by the chromosomes aligned at the cell's equator, equidistant from each pole.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At the onset of anaphase, each chromosome arranged at the metaphase plate is split simultaneously.
False 1: At the onset of telophase, each chromosome arranged at the metaphase plate is split simultaneously.
FIB 1: At the onset of anaphase, each ___ arranged at the metaphase plate is split simultaneously.
FIB 2: At the onset of anaphase, each chromosome arranged at the ___ plate is split simultaneously.
FIB 3: At the onset of anaphase, each chromosome arranged at the metaphase plate is split ___.
Reason: Centromere splitting at anaphase onset frees sister chromatids to move to opposite poles, triggered by the enzyme separase.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During anaphase, the two daughter chromatids begin their migration towards the two opposite poles.
False 1: During anaphase, the two daughter chromatids begin their migration towards the same pole.
FIB 1: During anaphase, the two daughter ___ begin their migration towards the two opposite poles.
FIB 2: During anaphase, the two daughter chromatids begin their migration ___ the two opposite poles.
FIB 3: During anaphase, the two daughter chromatids begin their migration towards the two ___ poles.
Reason: Sister chromatids move to opposite poles during anaphase, ensuring each daughter cell receives one copy of each chromosome.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome remains directed towards the pole at the leading edge, with the arms of the chromosome trailing behind.
False 1: During anaphase, the arms of each chromosome lead toward the pole, with the centromere trailing behind.
FIB 1: During anaphase, the ___ of each chromosome remains directed towards the pole at the leading edge, with the arms of the chromosome trailing behind.
FIB 2: During anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome remains directed towards the pole at the leading edge, with the arms of the ___ trailing behind.
FIB 3: During anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome remains directed towards the pole at the leading edge, with the arms of the chromosome ___ behind.
Reason: The centromere leads movement to the poles because spindle fibres shorten from the kinetochore end, pulling the chromosome centromere-first.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During anaphase, centromeres split and chromatids separate.
False 1: During metaphase, centromeres split and chromatids separate.
FIB 1: During anaphase, ___ split and chromatids separate.
FIB 2: During anaphase, centromeres split and ___ separate.
FIB 3: During anaphase, centromeres split and chromatids ___.
Reason: Centromere splitting releases the cohesin holding sister chromatids together, allowing them to be pulled to opposite poles.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At the beginning of telophase, the chromosomes that have reached their respective poles decondense and lose their individuality.
False 1: At the beginning of anaphase, the chromosomes that have reached their respective poles decondense and lose their individuality.
FIB 1: At the beginning of telophase, the chromosomes that have reached their ___ poles decondense and lose their individuality.
FIB 2: At the beginning of telophase, the chromosomes that have reached their respective poles ___ and lose their individuality.
FIB 3: At the beginning of telophase, the chromosomes that have reached their respective poles decondense and lose their ___.
Reason: At telophase, chromosomes have reached their poles and can now decondense back to chromatin for transcription in daughter cells.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At telophase, nuclear envelope develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole forming two daughter nuclei.
False 1: At metaphase, nuclear envelope develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole forming two daughter nuclei.
False 2: At telophase, nuclear envelope develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole forming four daughter nuclei.
FIB 1: At telophase, nuclear envelope develops around the ___ clusters at each pole forming two daughter nuclei.
FIB 2: At telophase, nuclear envelope develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole ___ two daughter nuclei.
FIB 3: At telophase, nuclear envelope develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole forming two ___ nuclei.
Reason: Nuclear envelope reforms in telophase around each chromosome cluster to isolate the genome from the cytoplasm and allow nuclear function.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At telophase, nucleolus, golgi complex and ER reform.
False 1: At prophase, nucleolus, golgi complex and ER reform.
FIB 1: At telophase, ___, golgi complex and ER reform.
FIB 2: At telophase, nucleolus, golgi ___ and ER reform.
FIB 3: At telophase, nucleolus, golgi complex and ___ reform.
Reason: Nucleolus, Golgi and ER reform at telophase because the daughter cells must resume normal protein synthesis and secretion.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Cytokinesis is the separation of cytoplasm at the end of which cell division gets completed.
False 1: Karyokinesis is the separation of cytoplasm at the end of which cell division gets completed.
FIB 1: ___ is the separation of cytoplasm at the end of which cell division gets completed.
FIB 2: Cytokinesis is the ___ of cytoplasm at the end of which cell division gets completed.
FIB 3: Cytokinesis is the separation of cytoplasm at the end of which cell division gets ___.
Reason: Cytokinesis is the physical division of the cytoplasm that completes cell division, separate from the nuclear division (karyokinesis).

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: In an animal cell, cytokinesis is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane.
False 1: In a plant cell, cytokinesis is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane.
FIB 1: In an animal cell, ___ is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane.
FIB 2: In an animal cell, cytokinesis is achieved by the ___ of a furrow in the plasma membrane.
FIB 3: In an animal cell, cytokinesis is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma ___.
Reason: Animal cells divide by ingrowth of the plasma membrane (cleavage furrow) because they lack a cell wall and are flexible.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls.
False 1: In plant cells, wall formation starts at the lateral walls and grows inward to meet at the centre of the cell.
FIB 1: In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows ___ to meet the existing lateral walls.
FIB 2: In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the ___ lateral walls.
FIB 3: In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing ___ walls.
Reason: Plant cell wall prevents furrow formation; instead, a new cell plate (future middle lamella) grows centrifugally from the phragmoplast.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells.
False 1: The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor called the cell-plate that represents the plasma membrane between the walls of two adjacent cells.
FIB 1: The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor called the ___ that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells.
FIB 2: The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor called the cell-plate that ___ the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells.
FIB 3: The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two ___ cells.
Reason: The cell plate forms the middle lamella between daughters and grows until it fuses with the existing lateral walls, partitioning the cell.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).
False 1: In some organisms cytokinesis is not followed by karyokinesis, leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).
FIB 1: In some organisms ___ is not followed by cytokinesis, leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).
FIB 2: In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by ___, leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in coconut).
FIB 3: In some organisms karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis, leading to the formation of syncytium (e.g., liquid endosperm in ___).
Reason: In some cases karyokinesis without cytokinesis creates a syncytium (many nuclei in shared cytoplasm), as in liquid coconut endosperm.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement.
False 1: Meiosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement.
FIB 1: ___ usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement.
FIB 2: Mitosis usually results in the ___ of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement.
FIB 3: Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic ___.
Reason: Mitosis produces diploid daughters with identical genetic material, preserving genome integrity for normal body function.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The growth of multicellular organisms is due to mitosis.
False 1: The growth of multicellular organisms is due to meiosis.
FIB 1: The growth of ___ organisms is due to mitosis.
FIB 2: The growth of multicellular ___ is due to mitosis.
FIB 3: The growth of multicellular organisms is due to ___.
Reason: Growth of multicellular organisms requires adding more cells with identical genomes through mitosis.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Cell growth results in disturbing the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
False 1: Cell division results in disturbing the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
FIB 1: Cell growth results in ___ the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
FIB 2: Cell growth results in disturbing the ratio between the ___ and the cytoplasm.
FIB 3: Cell growth results in disturbing the ratio between the nucleus and the ___.
Reason: As a cell grows, its volume increases faster than its surface area (cube vs. square relationship), disrupting the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: It becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
False 1: It becomes essential for the cell to grow further to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
FIB 1: It becomes ___ for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
FIB 2: It becomes essential for the cell to divide to ___ the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
FIB 3: It becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the ___ ratio.
Reason: Division restores the normal nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio so that the nucleus can adequately regulate cytoplasmic processes.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: A very significant contribution of mitosis is cell repair.
False 1: A very significant contribution of meiosis is cell repair.
FIB 1: A very ___ contribution of mitosis is cell repair.
FIB 2: A very significant ___ of mitosis is cell repair.
FIB 3: A very significant contribution of ___ is cell repair.
Reason: Mitosis replaces worn-out cells: epidermal cells shed, intestinal cells are lost to digestion, and red blood cells survive only ~120 days.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are being constantly replaced.
False 1: The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are rarely replaced.
FIB 1: The cells of the upper layer of the ___, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are being constantly replaced.
FIB 2: The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are being ___ replaced.
FIB 3: The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are being constantly ___.
Reason: Continuous cell loss in skin, gut and blood requires constant mitosis in stem cells to maintain tissue integrity.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Mitotic divisions in the meristematic tissues – the apical and the lateral cambium, result in a continuous growth of plants throughout their life.
False 1: Meiotic divisions in the meristematic tissues – the apical and the lateral cambium, result in a continuous growth of plants throughout their life.
FIB 1: Mitotic divisions in the ___ tissues – the apical and the lateral cambium, result in a continuous growth of plants throughout their life.
FIB 2: Mitotic divisions in the meristematic tissues – the apical and the lateral cambium, result in a ___ growth of plants throughout their life.
FIB 3: Mitotic divisions in the meristematic tissues – the apical and the lateral cambium, result in a continuous growth of plants ___ their life.
Reason: Meristematic cells (shoot/root apices, lateral cambium) remain mitotically active throughout a plant's life, enabling indeterminate growth.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Gametes are formed from specialised diploid cells.
False 1: Gametes are formed from specialised haploid cells.
FIB 1: ___ are formed from specialised diploid cells.
FIB 2: Gametes are formed from ___ diploid cells.
FIB 3: Gametes are formed from specialised ___ cells.
Reason: Specialised diploid cells (germline cells) undergo meiosis to produce haploid gametes, so fertilisation can restore the diploid number.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in the production of haploid daughter cells.
False 1: Mitosis reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in the production of haploid daughter cells.
False 2: Meiosis doubles the chromosome number, resulting in the production of diploid daughter cells.
FIB 1: ___ reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in the production of haploid daughter cells.
FIB 2: Meiosis reduces the ___ number by half, resulting in the production of haploid daughter cells.
FIB 3: Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half, resulting in the ___ of haploid daughter cells.
Reason: Meiosis halves chromosome number so that fertilisation of two haploid gametes restores the diploid number without doubling it each generation.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis ensures the production of haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms.
False 1: Fertilisation ensures the production of haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms.
FIB 1: ___ ensures the production of haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms.
FIB 2: Meiosis ensures the ___ of haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms.
FIB 3: Meiosis ensures the production of haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually ___ organisms.
Reason: Without meiosis, gametes would be diploid and fertilisation would double chromosome number each generation, which is unsustainable.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Fertilisation restores the diploid phase.
False 1: Meiosis restores the diploid phase.
FIB 1: ___ restores the diploid phase.
FIB 2: Fertilisation ___ the diploid phase.
FIB 3: Fertilisation restores the ___ phase.
Reason: Fertilisation restores the diploid number because two haploid gametes (n + n) combine to form a diploid zygote (2n).

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division called meiosis I and meiosis II but only a single cycle of DNA replication.
False 1: Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division called meiosis I and meiosis II and two cycles of DNA replication.
FIB 1: Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division called meiosis I and meiosis ___ but only a single cycle of DNA replication.
FIB 2: Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division called meiosis I and meiosis II but only a single cycle of ___ replication.
FIB 3: Meiosis involves two sequential cycles of nuclear and cell division called meiosis I and meiosis II but only a single cycle of DNA ___.
Reason: Meiosis uses a single round of DNA replication followed by two divisions to produce four haploid cells from one diploid cell.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis I is initiated after the parental chromosomes have replicated to produce identical sister chromatids at the S phase.
False 1: Meiosis II is initiated after the parental chromosomes have replicated to produce identical sister chromatids at the S phase.
FIB 1: Meiosis I is initiated after the parental ___ have replicated to produce identical sister chromatids at the S phase.
FIB 2: Meiosis I is initiated after the parental chromosomes have ___ to produce identical sister chromatids at the S phase.
FIB 3: Meiosis I is initiated after the parental chromosomes have replicated to produce identical sister ___ at the S phase.
Reason: Meiosis I must begin after S phase so that homologous chromosomes consist of two chromatids each, enabling crossing over between non-sister chromatids.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis involves pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
False 1: Mitosis involves pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
False 2: Meiosis involves pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
FIB 1: Meiosis involves pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between non-sister ___ of homologous chromosomes.
FIB 2: Meiosis involves pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between non-sister chromatids of ___ chromosomes.
FIB 3: Meiosis involves pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination between non-sister chromatids of homologous ___.
Reason: Crossing over (genetic recombination) occurs only in meiosis, not in mitosis, because homologous chromosomes must synapse for the exchange.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of meiosis II.
False 1: Two haploid cells are formed at the end of meiosis II.
False 2: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of meiosis I.
FIB 1: Four ___ cells are formed at the end of meiosis II.
FIB 2: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of ___ II.
FIB 3: Four haploid cells are formed at the end of meiosis ___.
Reason: Four haploid cells result from meiosis because two successive divisions (meiosis I + II) without intervening DNA replication halve the chromosome content twice.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Prophase I is typically longer and more complex when compared to prophase of mitosis.
False 1: Prophase I is typically shorter and simpler when compared to prophase of mitosis.
FIB 1: ___ I is typically longer and more complex when compared to prophase of mitosis.
FIB 2: Prophase I is typically longer and more complex when ___ to prophase of mitosis.
FIB 3: Prophase I is typically longer and more complex when compared to prophase of ___.
Reason: Prophase I is longer and more complex than mitotic prophase because it includes synapsis, synaptonemal complex formation and crossing over.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Prophase I has been further subdivided into five phases: Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and Diakinesis.
False 1: Prophase I has been further subdivided into four phases: Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, and Diplotene.
FIB 1: Prophase I has been further subdivided into five phases: Leptotene, Zygotene, ___, Diplotene and Diakinesis.
FIB 2: Prophase I has been further subdivided into five phases: Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, ___ and Diakinesis.
FIB 3: Prophase I has been further subdivided into five phases: Leptotene, Zygotene, Pachytene, Diplotene and ___.
Reason: Prophase I has five sub-stages (leptotene → zygotene → pachytene → diplotene → diakinesis) because synapsis, crossing over and chiasma resolution each require a distinct phase.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During leptotene stage, the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope.
False 1: During zygotene stage, the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light microscope.
FIB 1: During leptotene stage, the ___ become gradually visible under the light microscope.
FIB 2: During leptotene stage, the chromosomes become gradually ___ under the light microscope.
FIB 3: During leptotene stage, the chromosomes become gradually visible under the light ___.
Reason: During leptotene, chromosomes condense and become visible as they attach to the nuclear envelope, establishing their positions for synapsis.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During zygotene, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis.
False 1: During leptotene, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis.
False 2: During zygotene, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called crossing over.
FIB 1: During zygotene, ___ start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis.
FIB 2: During zygotene, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of ___ is called synapsis.
FIB 3: During zygotene, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called ___.
Reason: Synapsis during zygotene brings homologous chromosomes into precise alignment for crossing over.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Paired homologous chromosomes are called bivalents or tetrads.
False 1: Paired homologous chromosomes are called sister chromatids.
FIB 1: Paired ___ chromosomes are called bivalents or tetrads.
FIB 2: Paired homologous ___ are called bivalents or tetrads.
FIB 3: Paired homologous chromosomes are called bivalents or ___.
Reason: Paired homologous chromosomes are called bivalents (two chromosomes) or tetrads (four chromatids), both terms describing the same structure.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Chromosome synapsis is accompanied by the formation of a complex structure called synaptonemal complex.
False 1: Chromosome synapsis is accompanied by the formation of a complex structure called chiasmata.
FIB 1: ___ synapsis is accompanied by the formation of a complex structure called synaptonemal complex.
FIB 2: Chromosome synapsis is ___ by the formation of a complex structure called synaptonemal complex.
FIB 3: Chromosome synapsis is accompanied by the formation of a complex structure called ___ complex.
Reason: The synaptonemal complex is a protein scaffold that holds homologous chromosomes tightly together during synapsis, enabling crossing over.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad.
False 1: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a synaptonemal complex.
FIB 1: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed ___ chromosomes is called a bivalent or a tetrad.
FIB 2: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous ___ is called a bivalent or a tetrad.
FIB 3: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a ___ or a tetrad.
Reason: A bivalent/tetrad consists of two homologous chromosomes, each made of two sister chromatids, held together by the synaptonemal complex.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During pachytene, the four chromatids of each bivalent chromosome become distinct and clearly appear as tetrads.
False 1: During pachytene, the two chromatids of each bivalent chromosome become distinct.
FIB 1: During pachytene, the four ___ of each bivalent chromosome become distinct and clearly appear as tetrads.
FIB 2: During pachytene, the four chromatids of each bivalent ___ become distinct and clearly appear as tetrads.
FIB 3: During pachytene, the four chromatids of each bivalent chromosome become distinct and clearly appear as ___.
Reason: During pachytene, four chromatids become visible because the synaptonemal complex resolves enough to see all four chromatids of each bivalent.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Pachytene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes.
False 1: Diplotene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes.
False 2: Pachytene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes.
FIB 1: Pachytene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister ___ of the homologous chromosomes.
FIB 2: Pachytene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the ___ chromosomes.
FIB 3: Pachytene is characterised by the appearance of recombination nodules, the sites at which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous ___.
Reason: Recombination nodules on the synaptonemal complex mark the sites where recombinase enzyme machinery catalyses the actual crossing over.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes.
False 1: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two non-homologous chromosomes.
FIB 1: ___ over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes.
FIB 2: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two ___ chromosomes.
FIB 3: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous ___.
Reason: Crossing over at non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes shuffles alleles, generating new combinations not present in either parent.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Crossing over is an enzyme-mediated process and the enzyme involved is called recombinase.
False 1: Crossing over is an enzyme-mediated process and the enzyme involved is called synthetase.
FIB 1: ___ over is an enzyme-mediated process and the enzyme involved is called recombinase.
FIB 2: Crossing over is an ___ process and the enzyme involved is called recombinase.
FIB 3: Crossing over is an enzyme-mediated process and the enzyme involved is called ___.
Reason: Recombinase (like Spo11 and Rad51) catalyses the strand invasion steps that physically join and resolve non-sister chromatid segments.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Crossing over leads to recombination of genetic material on the two chromosomes.
False 1: Synapsis leads to recombination of genetic material on the two chromosomes.
FIB 1: ___ over leads to recombination of genetic material on the two chromosomes.
FIB 2: Crossing over leads to ___ of genetic material on the two chromosomes.
FIB 3: Crossing over leads to recombination of genetic material on the two ___.
Reason: Crossing over produces recombinant chromatids with allele combinations from both parents, increasing genetic diversity.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of pachytene.
False 1: Recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of zygotene.
FIB 1: ___ between homologous chromosomes is completed by the end of pachytene.
FIB 2: Recombination between ___ chromosomes is completed by the end of pachytene.
FIB 3: Recombination between homologous ___ is completed by the end of pachytene.
Reason: Recombination is completed by the end of pachytene, after which the chromosomes begin to separate at diplotene.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex.
False 1: The beginning of diakinesis is recognised by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex.
FIB 1: The beginning of diplotene is ___ by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex.
FIB 2: The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the ___ of the synaptonemal complex.
FIB 3: The beginning of diplotene is recognised by the dissolution of the ___ complex.
Reason: Synaptonemal complex dissolution at diplotene allows homologous chromosomes to begin separating except where chiasmata hold them.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During diplotene, the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents tend to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers.
False 1: During diplotene, the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents completely separate from each other including at the sites of crossovers.
FIB 1: During diplotene, the recombined ___ chromosomes of the bivalents tend to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers.
FIB 2: During diplotene, the recombined homologous ___ of the bivalents tend to separate from each other except at the sites of crossovers.
FIB 3: During diplotene, the recombined homologous chromosomes of the bivalents tend to separate from each other except at the sites of ___.
Reason: After crossing over, homologous chromosomes remain joined only at chiasmata (where exchanges occurred), keeping bivalents intact until anaphase I.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The X-shaped structures at crossover sites are called chiasmata.
False 1: The X-shaped structures at crossover sites are called synaptonemal complexes.
FIB 1: The ___ structures at crossover sites are called chiasmata.
FIB 2: The X-shaped ___ at crossover sites are called chiasmata.
FIB 3: The X-shaped structures at crossover sites are called ___.
Reason: Chiasmata form an X shape because a chromatid from one homologue is physically joined to a chromatid from the other homologue at the crossover point.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: In oocytes of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years.
False 1: In oocytes of some vertebrates, leptotene can last for months or years.
FIB 1: In ___ of some vertebrates, diplotene can last for months or years.
FIB 2: In oocytes of some ___, diplotene can last for months or years.
FIB 3: In oocytes of some vertebrates, ___ can last for months or years.
Reason: Prolonged diplotene in oocytes serves as a long pause during which the oocyte grows and accumulates maternal mRNAs and proteins.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Diakinesis is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata.
False 1: Diplotene is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata.
FIB 1: ___ is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata.
FIB 2: Diakinesis is marked by ___ of chiasmata.
FIB 3: Diakinesis is marked by terminalisation of ___.
Reason: Terminalisation (movement of chiasmata toward chromosome ends) in diakinesis releases tension and allows bivalents to separate fully.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: During diakinesis, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled.
False 1: During leptotene, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled.
FIB 1: During ___, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled.
FIB 2: During diakinesis, the ___ are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled.
FIB 3: During diakinesis, the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is ___.
Reason: At diakinesis, chromosomes are maximally condensed and spindle assembly begins, just as in the transition to metaphase in mitosis.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope also breaks down.
False 1: By the end of leptotene, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope also breaks down.
FIB 1: By the end of ___, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope also breaks down.
FIB 2: By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus ___ and the nuclear envelope also breaks down.
FIB 3: By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear ___ also breaks down.
Reason: Nucleolus and nuclear envelope break down at the end of diakinesis (as in mitotic prophase end) to allow spindle-chromosome interactions.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Diakinesis represents transition to metaphase.
False 1: Diplotene represents transition to metaphase.
FIB 1: ___ represents transition to metaphase.
FIB 2: Diakinesis ___ transition to metaphase.
FIB 3: Diakinesis represents ___ to metaphase.
Reason: Diakinesis is the final sub-stage of prophase I before metaphase I begins.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At metaphase I, the bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate.
False 1: At metaphase II, the bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate.
FIB 1: At metaphase I, the ___ chromosomes align on the equatorial plate.
FIB 2: At metaphase I, the bivalent ___ align on the equatorial plate.
FIB 3: At metaphase I, the bivalent chromosomes align on the ___ plate.
Reason: At metaphase I, bivalents (not individual chromosomes) align on the equatorial plate because homologous chromosomes have not yet separated.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At metaphase I, the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle attach to the kinetochore of homologous chromosomes.
False 1: At metaphase I, the microtubules from the same pole of the spindle attach to the kinetochore of homologous chromosomes.
FIB 1: At metaphase I, the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle attach to the ___ of homologous chromosomes.
FIB 2: At metaphase I, the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle attach to the kinetochore of ___ chromosomes.
FIB 3: At metaphase I, the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle attach to the kinetochore of homologous ___.
Reason: Microtubules from opposite poles attach to homologous chromosomes (not sister chromatids) at metaphase I, so pulling them apart in anaphase I.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes separate, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres.
False 1: At anaphase II, the homologous chromosomes separate, while sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres.
False 2: At anaphase I, the sister chromatids separate, while homologous chromosomes remain associated at their centromeres.
FIB 1: At anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes separate, while sister ___ remain associated at their centromeres.
FIB 2: At anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes separate, while sister chromatids remain ___ at their centromeres.
FIB 3: At anaphase I, the homologous chromosomes separate, while sister chromatids remain associated at their ___.
Reason: At anaphase I, homologous chromosomes (each still a pair of sister chromatids) move to opposite poles; sister chromatids separate only in meiosis II.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At telophase I, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear, cytokinesis follows and this is called dyad of cells.
False 1: At telophase II, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear, cytokinesis follows and this is called dyad of cells.
FIB 1: At telophase I, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus ___, cytokinesis follows and this is called dyad of cells.
FIB 2: At telophase I, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear, ___ follows and this is called dyad of cells.
FIB 3: At telophase I, the nuclear membrane and nucleolus reappear, cytokinesis ___ and this is called dyad of cells.
Reason: After telophase I and cytokinesis, two haploid cells (dyad) are produced, each with n chromosomes as bivalents, ready for meiosis II.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The stage between the two meiotic divisions is called interkinesis.
False 1: The stage between the two meiotic divisions is called interphase.
FIB 1: The stage between the two ___ divisions is called interkinesis.
FIB 2: The stage between the two meiotic ___ is called interkinesis.
FIB 3: The stage between the two meiotic divisions is called ___.
Reason: Interkinesis is the brief rest period separating meiosis I from meiosis II; it differs from interphase in having no S phase.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: There is no replication of DNA during interkinesis.
False 1: There is no replication of DNA during interphase.
FIB 1: There is no ___ of DNA during interkinesis.
FIB 2: There is no replication of ___ during interkinesis.
FIB 3: There is no replication of DNA during ___.
Reason: Interkinesis has no DNA replication because the genetic content must not be doubled again between the two meiotic divisions.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Interkinesis is followed by prophase II, a much simpler prophase than prophase I.
False 1: Interkinesis is followed by prophase II, a much more complex prophase than prophase I.
FIB 1: ___ is followed by prophase II, a much simpler prophase than prophase I.
FIB 2: Interkinesis is followed by prophase ___, a much simpler prophase than prophase I.
FIB 3: Interkinesis is followed by prophase II, a much simpler prophase than ___ I.
Reason: Prophase II is simpler than prophase I because there is no synapsis or crossing over in meiosis II — it resembles mitotic prophase.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis II is initiated immediately after cytokinesis.
False 1: Meiosis I is initiated immediately after cytokinesis.
FIB 1: Meiosis ___ is initiated immediately after cytokinesis.
FIB 2: Meiosis II is initiated ___ after cytokinesis.
FIB 3: Meiosis II is initiated immediately after ___.
Reason: Meiosis II begins immediately after cytokinesis because the cells must proceed to further halve their genetic content without delay.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II resembles a normal mitosis.
False 1: In contrast to meiosis II, meiosis I resembles a normal mitosis.
FIB 1: In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis ___ resembles a normal mitosis.
FIB 2: In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II ___ a normal mitosis.
FIB 3: In contrast to meiosis I, meiosis II resembles a normal ___.
Reason: Meiosis II resembles mitosis because it separates sister chromatids, just as mitosis does, but in already-haploid cells.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of prophase II.
False 1: The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of metaphase II.
FIB 1: The nuclear membrane ___ by the end of prophase II.
FIB 2: The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of ___ II.
FIB 3: The nuclear membrane disappears by the end of prophase ___.
Reason: Nuclear envelope breaks down at the end of prophase II (as in mitotic prophase), allowing spindle microtubules to access chromosomes.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: At metaphase II, the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the kinetochores of sister chromatids.
False 1: At metaphase II, the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the kinetochores of homologous chromosomes.
FIB 1: At metaphase ___, the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the kinetochores of sister chromatids.
FIB 2: At metaphase II, the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the ___ of sister chromatids.
FIB 3: At metaphase II, the chromosomes align at the equator and the microtubules from opposite poles of the spindle get attached to the kinetochores of sister ___.
Reason: In meiosis II, microtubules from opposite poles attach to sister chromatids at metaphase II, mirroring the kinetochore attachment of mitosis.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Anaphase II begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome, allowing sister chromatids to move toward opposite poles.
False 1: Anaphase I begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome, allowing sister chromatids to move toward opposite poles.
FIB 1: Anaphase ___ begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome, allowing sister chromatids to move toward opposite poles.
FIB 2: Anaphase II begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each ___, allowing sister chromatids to move toward opposite poles.
FIB 3: Anaphase II begins with the simultaneous splitting of the centromere of each chromosome, allowing sister ___ to move toward opposite poles.
Reason: Centromere splitting at anaphase II releases sister chromatids to opposite poles, completing the separation of all genetic material.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis ends with telophase II, resulting in the formation of tetrad of cells, i.e., four haploid daughter cells.
False 1: Meiosis ends with telophase II, resulting in the formation of a dyad of two cells.
False 2: Meiosis ends with telophase I, resulting in the formation of tetrad of cells, i.e., four haploid daughter cells.
FIB 1: ___ ends with telophase II, resulting in the formation of tetrad of cells, i.e., four haploid daughter cells.
FIB 2: Meiosis ends with telophase ___, resulting in the formation of tetrad of cells, i.e., four haploid daughter cells.
FIB 3: Meiosis ends with telophase II, resulting in the formation of tetrad of cells, i.e., four haploid ___ cells.
Reason: Meiosis II ends with telophase II, producing four haploid cells (tetrad) because two cells each divide into two.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis is the mechanism by which conservation of specific chromosome number of each species is achieved across generations.
False 1: Mitosis is the mechanism by which conservation of specific chromosome number of each species is achieved across generations.
FIB 1: Meiosis is the mechanism by which ___ of specific chromosome number of each species is achieved across generations.
FIB 2: Meiosis is the mechanism by which conservation of specific ___ number of each species is achieved across generations.
FIB 3: Meiosis is the mechanism by which conservation of specific chromosome number of each species is achieved across ___.
Reason: Meiosis maintains constant chromosome number across generations by producing haploid gametes that, when fertilised, restore the diploid number.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Meiosis increases the genetic variability in the population of organisms from one generation to the next.
False 1: Meiosis decreases the genetic variability in the population of organisms from one generation to the next.
FIB 1: Meiosis increases the genetic ___ in the population of organisms from one generation to the next.
FIB 2: Meiosis increases the genetic variability in the ___ of organisms from one generation to the next.
FIB 3: Meiosis increases the genetic variability in the population of organisms from one ___ to the next.
Reason: Crossing over and random assortment of homologous chromosomes at meiosis I generate immense genetic variation in the gametes produced.

Chapter: 11th Ch10 - Cell Cycle and Cell Division
True Statement: Variations are very important for the process of evolution.
False 1: Variations are unimportant for the process of evolution.
FIB 1: ___ are very important for the process of evolution.
FIB 2: Variations are very important for the ___ of evolution.
FIB 3: Variations are very important for the process of ___.
Reason: Genetic variation is essential for natural selection and evolution; without variation there is no raw material for evolution to act upon.
